bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Minimum Wage QLD and Your Pay Conversion

If you're paid by the hour or considering a salary offer, converting your hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, or weekly figures helps you compare offers and plan your budget. This guide explains the standard formula, how casual loading and superannuation work, and what the **minimum wage qld** means for your calculations.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours per Week × 52

The standard conversion is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

We assume a 38-hour week for full-time work, as that is the ordinary hours under the Fair Work Act. If your hours differ, adjust accordingly. For example, a 20-hour week would use 20 instead of 38.

Using the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026), the annual gross for 38 hours is:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,265.44

Your weekly pay is $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.72 (matching the Fair Work Ombudsman's $1,004.90 figure, rounded). Your fortnightly pay is twice that: $2,009.44.

### What Is the Minimum Wage QLD?

The National Minimum Wage set by the Fair Work Commission applies across Australia, including Queensland. As of 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. However, many employees are covered by awards or enterprise agreements that set higher minimum rates. The **minimum wage qld** for a specific job may be higher than the national baseline, so always check your award or agreement. For a broader overview, see our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page.

### Casual Loading: Adding 25% on Top

Casual employees receive a loading of 25% on their base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave (annual leave, sick leave, etc.). The casual rate for the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour.

When using our [timesheet](/), do **not** type a rate that already includes casual loading. Instead, enter your base hourly rate and tick the 'casual loading' checkbox. The tool will add the 25% automatically. This ensures you see the correct breakdown of base pay and loading.

For a casual worker on the minimum wage, the annual gross (38 hours, 52 weeks) becomes:

$33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,331.80

That's $1,256.38 per week or $2,512.76 per fortnight.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top of Your Gross Pay

Super guarantee is currently 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer **on top** of your gross pay. It is not deducted from your hourly rate. For a full-time employee on the National Minimum Wage, the employer contributes an extra:

12% × $52,265.44 = $6,271.85 per year

This contribution stops once your earnings reach the maximum contribution base of $270,830 (2026–27). Super is not included in the hourly-to-annual conversion because it is an additional employer cost, not part of your take-home pay. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Tax and Medicare

Your annual gross pay is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For 2026–27, the resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15c for each $1 over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30c for each $1 over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37c for each $1 over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,370 plus 45c for each $1 over $190,000

The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. The single reduction thresholds for 2026–27 were not confirmed at the time of this guide, so we use the 2025–26 thresholds. This estimate does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

### Award Rates vs. National Minimum Wage

Many workers in Queensland are covered by modern awards that set higher minimum rates than the National Minimum Wage. For example, the Hospitality Industry (General) Award or the Retail Award have specific hourly rates for different classifications. Always check your award or enterprise agreement. For award-specific guidance, refer to our [pay guides](/blog) page.

### Average Earnings in Queensland

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports average weekly earnings. For Queensland full-time adult ordinary time in May 2026, the average was $2,039.70 per week. This is an **average** across all industries and occupations, not the median for any specific job. It can help you benchmark, but your actual rate depends on your role, experience, and award.

### Using the Timesheet for Your Conversion

Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and choose whether you are casual. It calculates annual, fortnightly, weekly, and monthly figures, plus an estimate of tax and super. Remember:

- Enter your base rate (without casual loading).
- Tick the casual loading checkbox if applicable.
- The tool assumes 38 hours per week unless you change it.
- Results are estimates only, not a determination of your actual pay.

### Summary

Converting your hourly rate to annual pay is straightforward: multiply by hours per week and 52. The **minimum wage qld** is the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, but many workers earn more under awards. Casual loading adds 25% on top, and super is an additional 12% paid by your employer. Use our tools to see your figures, and always check your specific award or agreement for the correct rate. For more on casual loading, visit our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page.

**Disclaimer:** Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
